title: Liver failure, portal hypertension and bile duct disease
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's liver or bile duct condition.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for primary biliary cholangitis.

HPI
The patient is a 79-year-old woman who presents today for a scheduled follow-up regarding her primary biliary cholangitis. She has been under the care of a hepatologist and is currently managed on ursodiol. She reports feeling generally well today and denies any significant fatigue, pruritus, or joint pain. She notes that she has been adherent to her medication regimen. She reports that her energy levels have been stable over the last month. She denies any new symptoms or concerns related to her liver health.

Review of Systems
The patient denies fever, chills, weight loss, or night sweats. She denies any new onset of itching or jaundice. She reports no shortness of breath or chest pain. She denies any recent changes in bowel habits or urinary frequency.

Social History
She lives at home with her spouse and reports being retired. She enjoys gardening and walking in her neighborhood. She denies tobacco use and reports a balanced diet.

Family History
Her mother had hypertension and her father had type 2 diabetes. No family history of significant liver disease is reported.

Vitals
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 128/78 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air
Height: 5'4"
Weight: 155 lbs

Recent Labs
ALT: 45 U/L
AST: 38 U/L
ALP: 180 U/L
Total Bilirubin: 0.9 mg/dL
eGFR: 62 mL/min/1.73m2

Medication List
Ursodiol 300 mg daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. She appears in no acute distress. Her skin is clear without jaundice or significant itching. Her mucous membranes are moist. Abdominal exam reveals a soft, non-tender abdomen with no palpable masses or organomegaly. Lungs are clear to auscultation.

Assessment
The patient is a 79-year-old woman with primary biliary cholangitis. She is currently stable on ursodiol. Recent laboratory results indicate improving liver tests, specifically showing a downward trend in alkaline phosphatase and transaminase levels.

Plan
Continue current dose of ursodiol. Follow up with the hepatologist in three months for repeat laboratory monitoring. Encourage continued monitoring of energy levels and any new symptoms.

Electronically signed, D. Kowalski, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Primary biliary cholangitis (formerly primary biliary cirrhosis): K74.3 (HCC 68).
